name: MONTENEGRO

flag.title: Montenegro
flag.note: Red field, gold border, eagle crest

lead: Montenegro is in the western Balkans, in southeast Europe. Tall mountains drop into the Adriatic Sea. It is one of Europe's newest countries. It is smaller than Connecticut. Swim in a warm bay, then hike past glacial lakes (lakes made by ancient ice).
geo: Over 70% of Montenegro is mountain. Rough limestone peaks and deep, narrow valleys fill the land. The Durmitor range has 18 glacial lakes, called 'mountain eyes'.
The coast is only 293 km long. The Bay of Kotor cuts deep inland. Lake Skadar, on the Albanian border, is the biggest lake in the Balkans.
animals: About 300 brown bears roam the forests of the Durmitor and Prokletije mountains. Wolves and Eurasian lynx live there too.
About 300 Dalmatian pelicans nest on floating reed islands at Lake Skadar. It is one of the world's biggest pelican colonies. Griffon vultures soar above Tara Canyon.
culture: Njeguški pršut is mountain ham. It dries for months in the cool winds of Njeguši village. People eat it with hard sheep's cheese.
Montenegrins are proud. A saying goes: 'There are few of us, but we are strong'. Long poems about warrior heroes were sung here for centuries.
history: Montenegro held off the Ottoman Empire (a huge Turkish empire) for centuries. Mountain warriors used the rough land to stop bigger armies. It was never fully conquered.
In 2006 Montenegro voted to leave its union with Serbia. The result was 55.5%. It just passed the 55% needed.
wows: Both 'Monte Negro' and 'Crna Gora' mean Black Mountain, the only country name with 'mountain'.
Tara Canyon is 1,300 m deep, Europe's deepest gorge and second only to the Grand Canyon.
Montenegro chose the euro on its own in 2002 but is not in the EU.
Cetinje had the first Balkan Slavic printing press in 1493, early even for Europe.
It has more UNESCO-protected land per km² than almost any European nation.
Bears, wolves and lynx still roam wild, which is rare in Western Europe.
People bungee jump from the 172 m Đurđevića Tara Bridge, built in 1940.

myths.fact: It is a ria, a drowned river valley. Glaciers never reached this warm coast.
Bears doze lightly and wake easily. Mothers even give birth in the den.
